name: Split Cord Malformation Type II
aliases: Split Cord Malformation without Bony Spur

criteria.description: Presence of two hemicords within a single dural sac without an osseous or cartilaginous septum
MRI evidence demonstrating split cord morphology and absence of bony spur
Identification of tethered cord or associated spinal dysraphism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Both major criteria (cord duplication within a single dural sac and MRI confirmation without bony spur) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from Type I split cord malformation requires absence of bony or cartilaginous septum

pathognomonic.symptomName: Split spinal cord within a single dural sac
pathognomonic.notes: Defining anatomical feature seen on imaging
searchTerms: spinal cord split within one dural sac
single covering with divided spinal cord

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental neurological deficits corresponding to hemicord involvement
searchTerms: nerve deficits matching one half of spinal cord
segmental weakness or numbness on one side
abnormal sensations in feet and legs

common.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urinary retention or incontinence
searchTerms: bladder problems like retention or leakage

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata over the spine such as hairy patches or dimples
searchTerms: hairy patches or skin dimples over spine
cutaneous spinal markers like hair tufts or pits

occasional.symptomName: Back pain localized to the affected spinal segment
searchTerms: back pain at affected spinal segment

occasional.symptomName: Gait abnormalities including spasticity or ataxia
searchTerms: walking problems with stiffness or unsteady gait
gait abnormalities including spastic or uncoordinated walking
difficulty walking due to muscle tone or balance issues
loss of muscle mass in lower limbs

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous hemangiomas overlying the spinal lesion
searchTerms: skin blood vessel tumors over spinal lesion

imaging: MRI demonstrating two hemicords within a single dural sac without bony or cartilaginous septum
Ultrasound in infants showing split cord morphology
CT scan to exclude bony spur presence
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence predominates
other: Intraoperative findings confirming absence of bony spur and presence of fibrous septum

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of bony or cartilaginous septum dividing the two hemicords
Cord tethering without split cord morphology
Symptoms related to cord traction without duplicated cord

redFlags: Rapid onset bladder or bowel dysfunction
Severe spinal deformity with neurological compromise
references: Pang D. Split cord malformation: Part I: A unified theory of embryogenesis for double spinal cord malformations. Neurosurgery. 1992.
Kumar R, et al. MRI features of split cord malformations. Indian J Radiol Imaging. 2014.
Orphanet: Split cord malformation type II (ORPHA:573253)
